title: Interim: borrow the serial port for flashing under conserver
description: Until OTA lands, conserver and espflash both want /dev/ttyUSB0 exclusively. Provide flash-under-conserver.sh (stop or down conserver, espflash flash, restore) wired as the cargo runner or a make target so cargo run transparently borrows the port; document conserver native down/up (Ctrl-E c d then o) as the lighter alternative. Superseded by the OTA epic once flashing no longer needs the UART.

title: OTA-over-WiFi firmware updates
description: Give the M5StickC Plus firmware-update-over-WiFi so flashing no longer needs exclusive ownership of /dev/ttyUSB0, which collides with a shared serial console (conserver). Board is confirmed capable: ESP32-PICO-D4, 2.4GHz WiFi, 4MB flash; the factory partition table already carries otadata and the ESP-IDF second-stage bootloader honors A/B OTA slots. Target stack pinned to latest (mid-2026): esp-hal 1.1, esp-radio (WiFi, successor to esp-wifi), esp-rtos (scheduler, successor to esp-hal-embassy), esp-storage plus esp-bootloader-esp-idf (flash writes plus otadata/rollback), embassy-net (TCP). Endgame: images push over the network into the inactive OTA slot and the UART is freed for a permanent shared console. led-core stays framework-free; OTA is a new use case behind ports. See the KB finding on the esp-rs version/compat matrix.

title: Own the WS2812 RMT encoder; move firmware to esp-hal 1.1
description: esp-hal-smartled pins esp-hal ~1.0, capping the firmware below the 1.1 floor the WiFi/OTA stack requires. Replace it with an in-tree WS2812 encoder driven directly off the esp-hal 1.1 RMT peripheral, implementing the domain LedOutput port, and drop the smart-leds/rgb deps. Wire behaviour must be unchanged (datasheet WS2812 tick counts, same as smartled). Acceptance: firmware builds on the esp toolchain AND the strip renders correctly on the board -- a clean build is not sufficient, on-wire timing must be confirmed visually or with a scope.

title: Async runtime: esp-rtos executor + esp-alloc heap
description: WiFi and embassy-net are async and need an executor and a heap. Stand up esp-rtos (features esp32, embassy, esp-radio) as the scheduler -- it supersedes esp-hal-embassy, which is frozen on the 1.0 line -- and esp-alloc for the global allocator. Convert the blocking render loop into an embassy task on embassy-time (a 20ms tick), keeping led-core synchronous and untouched. Acceptance: builds and the LED animation still runs under the executor on the board.

title: WiFi STA bring-up via esp-radio
description: Join a 2.4GHz AP as a station and obtain a DHCP lease via embassy-net, using esp-radio (features wifi, esp-alloc; needs the esp-rtos rtos-driver). Credentials must not be committed -- read from build-time env or a git-ignored config. Acceptance: the board logs an acquired IP and resolves DNS. Needs the board and AP credentials.

title: Dual-OTA partition table + otadata/slot writer
description: Adopt firmware/partitions.csv (dual ota_0/ota_1, 4MB) via espflash --partition-table and update the runner/flash docs. Use esp-bootloader-esp-idf to read the partition table and otadata (active slot, mark valid/invalid for rollback) and esp-storage to write the inactive slot. Acceptance: read the current boot slot at runtime and write-plus-verify an image into the other slot on the board (image may come from a flash read or embedded blob at this stage; no network yet). Flashing this table overwrites the factory app -- factory image is backed up in KB.

title: OTA update use case: fetch image, flip slot, roll back on failure
description: The update flow as a domain use case. Add a port for the firmware-image source and a control (FirmwareUpdate) that fetches an image over embassy-net (HTTP pull from a homelab URL), streams it into the inactive OTA slot, validates it, sets otadata to boot the new slot, and reboots; a failed boot rolls back via the bootloader. The transport is an adapter; the update policy (whether/when to update, version check) lives in the domain. Acceptance: an image served from the homelab is pulled and booted end-to-end, and a deliberately-bad image rolls back.

title: OTA runbook + KB; free the UART for a permanent console
description: Document how to build and publish an OTA image, trigger an update, and verify/observe it (partition map, otadata semantics, rollback) as a KB guide plus finding. Once OTA is the update path, wire the permanent shared serial console (conserver owns /dev/ttyUSB0 for good) and update kb/guides/sharing-the-serial-console.md -- the flash contention is resolved because flashing no longer touches the UART. Cross-link serial-open-resets-esp32.
